newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean prices crash to record low.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean prices crash to record low.

text.p: Indian soybean prices on Monday crashed to a record low, falling by 1,000 rupees per tonne to 10,100 rupees on poor demand, traders said.

They said soybean prices fell in the range of 1,000-1,100 rupees per tonne to 10,100-10,500 rupees as there was an oversupply situation and most processing plants have been shut in the past two months due to little work.
One trader said the ones that were running were operating at 10-20 capacity, mainly to meet export needs.

"Prices may further decrease by at least 500 rupees per tonne tomorrow as demand is very poor. Soybean prices may touch the November 1996 price levels -- 9,500-9,700 rupees per tonne in central Indian markets," one trader said.
According to some unofficial estimates, around 700,000 tonnes soybean stock is with farmers and around 50,000 tonnes soybean is with traders and processors.
